```{r}

hmm.traj <- nimbleCode({
 
  # Prior
  ## Transition
  phi.S ~ dunif(0, 1)
  phi.NS ~ dunif(0, 1)
 
  ## Speed
  mean.S ~ dunif(5, 40)  # Prior shape Gamma distribution (distance) : in-search
  sd.S ~ dunif(0.01, 50)   # Prior scale Gamma distribution (distance) : in-search
  mean.NS ~ dunif(40, 100) # Prior shape Gamma distribution (distance) : in-transit
  sd.NS ~ dunif(0.01, 50)  # Prior scale Gamma distribution (distance) : in-transit
   
  ## Initial state probability
  delta[1] <- 0.5
  delta[2] <- 0.5
 
  # Transition matrix
  gamma[1,1] <- phi.S      # Pr(in-search t -> in-search t+1)
  gamma[1,2] <- 1 - phi.S  # Pr(in-search t -> in-transit t+1)
  gamma[2,1] <- 1 - phi.NS # Pr(in-transit t -> in-search t+1)
  gamma[2,2] <- phi.NS     # Pr(in-transit t -> in-transit t+1)

  # Speed matrix
  speed[1,1] <- mean.S
  speed[1,2] <- sd.S
  speed[2,1] <- mean.NS
  speed[2,2] <- sd.NS

  # Likelihood
  ## Iteration over individuals
  for (i in 1:N) {
    z[i,first[i]] ~ dcat(delta[1:2])

    y[i, first[i]] ~ dgamma(mean = speed[z[i,first[i]],1], sd = speed[z[i,first[i]],2])                
     
    ### Iteration over time

    for (t in (first[i]+1):last[i]) {
      z[i,t] ~ dcat(gamma[z[i,t-1],1:2])
     
      y[i, t] ~ dgamma(mean = speed[z[i,t],1], sd = speed[z[i,t],2])

     
    } # t
  } # i
 
})
```



Get the date of first location.
```{r}

first <- apply(y, 1, function(x) min(which(!is.na(x))))
last <- apply(y, 1, function(x) max(which(!is.na(x))))
```


Specification of the constants and the data
```{r}

(my.constants <- list(N = nrow(y),
                      first = first,
                      last = last))

speed <- matrix(c(60, 30,
                5, 5), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)

my.data <- list(y = y,
                speed = speed)
```


Let's write a function for the initial values
```{r}


z.init <- y
for (i in 1:nrow(y)) {
  for (j in first[i]:ncol(y)) {
    if (!is.na(y[i,j])){
    z.init[i,j] <- rcat(1, c(0.5,0.5))

    }
  }
}

mean.init <- z.init
sd.init <- z.init
for (i in 1:nrow(z.init)) {
  for (j in first[i]:last[i]) {
    if (z.init[i,j] == 1){

      mean.init[i,j] <- 30
      sd.init[i,j] <- 5
    } else if (z.init[i,j] == 2){

      mean.init[i,j] <- 60
      sd.init[i,j] <- 5
    }
  }
}

initial.values <- function() list(phi.S = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  phi.NS = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  mean.S = 30,
                                  mean.NS = 60,
                                  sd.S = 5,
                                  sd.NS = 5,
                                  z = z.init)
```


We specify the parameters we'd like to monitor
```{r}

(parameters.to.save <- c("phi.S", "phi.NS",
                        "mean.S", "mean.NS",
                        "sd.S", "sd.NS"))
```

We try the model
```{r}
mod.traj <- nimbleModel(code = hmm.traj,
                          constants = my.constants,
                          data = my.data,
                          inits = initial.values())

Hi Rémy,

I'm not quite understanding what your question is here. Let me make a few comments and then hopefully that will help us to understand each other better.

1) the lifted variables that are of dimension 6x13 are created by reparameterizing the gamma distribution from {mean, sd} to {shape, scale} for the second `y` declaration in the model. The lifted variables associated with `y` will have N=6 rows and as many columns as the largest value of `last` (which seems to be 13 in this case).
      a) for this case the first column is not used because `y[ , 1]` is not defined by that declaration, so the corresponding lifted values are missing.
      b) it looks like `first` is 1 for all individuals and `last` is 13 for all individuals. For any element of `y` that corresponds to a value before `first[i]+1` or after `last[i]`, the value of the corresponding lifted variable will be NA, since it will correspond to a non-existent `y` node in the model. So if `first[i]` is 1, then one gets an NA at the [i,1] position for the lifted variable (as you see)(. If `first[i]` is 2 then one also gets an NA at the [i,2] position for the lifted variable (not seen in your case).
2) the lifted variables that are vectors of length 6 are created by reparameterizing  the gamma distribution for the first `y` declaration. There are no NAs here, because these correspond to the value of `y` for the first observation for each individual.

If what I said above doesn't help, please provide me with the `y` values you are using so I can fully reproduce this. As a side note, you don't need to provide `speed` as part of `data` because `speed` is deterministically set based on other quantities in the model.

-chris

hmm.traj <- nimbleCode({
 
  # Prior
  ## Transition
  phi.S ~ dunif(0, 1)
  phi.NS ~ dunif(0, 1)
 
  ## Speed
  mean.S ~ dunif(5, 40)  # Prior shape Gamma distribution (distance) : in-search
  sd.S ~ dunif(0.01, 50)   # Prior scale Gamma distribution (distance) : in-search
  mean.NS ~ dunif(40, 100) # Prior shape Gamma distribution (distance) : in-transit
  sd.NS ~ dunif(0.01, 50)  # Prior scale Gamma distribution (distance) : in-transit
   
  ## Initial state probability
  delta[1] <- 0.5
  delta[2] <- 0.5
 
  # Transition matrix
  gamma[1,1] <- phi.S      # Pr(in-search t -> in-search t+1)
  gamma[1,2] <- 1 - phi.S  # Pr(in-search t -> in-transit t+1)
  gamma[2,1] <- 1 - phi.NS # Pr(in-transit t -> in-search t+1)
  gamma[2,2] <- phi.NS     # Pr(in-transit t -> in-transit t+1)

  # Speed matrix
  speed[1,1] <- mean.S
  speed[1,2] <- sd.S
  speed[2,1] <- mean.NS
  speed[2,2] <- sd.NS

  # Likelihood
  ## Iteration over individuals
  for (i in 1:N) {
    z[i,first[i]] ~ dcat(delta[1:2])

    y[i, first[i]] ~ dgamma(mean = speed[z[i,first[i]],1], sd = speed[z[i,first[i]],2])                
     
    ### Iteration over time

    for (t in (first[i]+1):last[i]) {
      z[i,t] ~ dcat(gamma[z[i,t-1],1:2])
     
      y[i, t] ~ dgamma(mean = speed[z[i,t],1], sd = speed[z[i,t],2])

     
    } # t
  } # i
 
})
